role: Crash-safety net for raw RR beats: writes every recording's beats to RRBackup/ in the App Group container (one-shot encrypted single-file JSON, or append-only header+JSONL via RawRRBackup+Streaming.swift), keeps a JSON index of backups, and serves retrieve/list/discard/purge/reconcile APIs to recovery, archive and diagnostics code.
types: RawRRBackup: class (@unchecked Sendable) — raw RR backup store; extended by RawRRBackup+Streaming.swift, RawRRBackup+IndexRecovery.swift and SessionStorageDiagnostic.swift
RawRRBackup.BackupEntry: struct (Codable) — decoded backup (id, captureDate, deviceId, points, hash)
RawRRBackup.BackupHeader: struct (Codable) — header file of the append-only format
RawRRBackup.BackupIndex: struct (Codable) — index row (fileName for one-shot, backedUpCount for append-only, archived flag, lastBackupTime) with schemaVersion key
RawRRBackup.TerminationForensicsSummary: struct — static lockless view of one index row for CrashLogManager
state: file:{AppGroup group.com.chrissharp.flowrecovery or Documents or tmp}/RRBackup/ (AppConfig.backupDirectoryName)
file:RRBackup/<uuid>_<unixtime>.json (one-shot backup, encrypted when EncryptionManager available)
toplevel: Stored-property initializers: index = [], indexReadFailed = false, fileManager = FileManager.default, indexLock = NSLock(), appendQueue serial utility queue, lineEncoder closure (82). BackupIndex declares CodingKeys including schemaVersion. The class is @unchecked Sendable relying on indexLock + appendQueue; only incrementalBackup and resetInMemoryStateAfterPurge/reencryptPendingBackups run on appendQueue — backup(), markAsArchived, discardBackup, reconcile*, purge mutate index under indexLock only.

Returns the entry.

flags.text: The 'never replace a larger backup' guard (317) only sees the in-memory index. When the index file could not be read at launch (loadIndex sets indexReadFailed and leaves index empty, RawRRBackup+Streaming.swift:328-331, e.g. a launch before first unlock), existing is nil, so backup() for an interrupted night's id writes the shorter one-shot file and cleanupAppendFiles (326) deletes the streamed header/points files and .corrupted_* siblings holding more beats; mergeIndexThatFailedToLoad later lets the new in-memory row win (Streaming:359).

Order of effects: append-only files are deleted (326) before the new index row is persisted (327 → saveIndex 465). If saveIndex throws (write failure, or mergeIndexThatFailedToLoad still cannot read the file, Streaming:356), backup() throws but the on-disk index keeps the old append-format row whose files are gone and no on-disk row references the new one-shot file; recoverIndexFromFiles only runs on a decode failure (Streaming:346).

units.does: SHA-256 hex digest of the points encoded as JSON with sorted keys and iso8601 dates, inside an autoreleasepool.

Encodes the entry (encrypted when possible), records/clears the session in the raw-backup PendingEncryptionLedger, then writes bytes with .completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication when encrypted, .completeFileProtection when plaintext.

branches.effect: true: until-first-auth protection; false: complete protection

flags.text: Write is not .atomic; reencryptBackup (417) rewrites the only copy of a one-shot backup in place, so a kill mid-write leaves a truncated file and the backup no longer decodes.

Doc comment says the plaintext append-only points file is 'encrypted at the directory level via NSFileProtectionComplete (set in createBackupDirectoryIfNeeded)', but that function sets .completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication (Streaming:260) and the points/header writes use the same class (Streaming:45,55,92), so raw RR stays readable whenever the device has been unlocked once since boot.
